summary: Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at Indiana and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and others, later teaching at Macalester, Hawaiʻi, Stanford, Indiana (1992–2005), and Soka University (2004–2010).

Linguist Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay studied at Warsaw, Leipzig under August Leskien, Berlin, and Charles University. He held positions at Kazan Imperial University (c. 1874–1883), Tartu (1883–1893), Jagiellonian University (1893–1900), and Saint Petersburg State University (c. 1900–1918).

Jan P. Hogendijk specializes in the history of science and Indology. He completed his promotion at Utrecht University in 1983 and has held posts at Frankfurt, Utrecht (from 1986; professor from 2005), and Leiden University (2004–2009).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper and studied under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Westerhoff specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his BA and PhD at Cambridge under Michael Potter and a PhD at SOAS. He held posts at Durham and Oxford, where he is Professor of Buddhist Philosophy.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University and studied with Walter Eugene Clark and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at Leiden (1950–1956) and the Australian National University (1965–1986).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. He held a professorship at the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006) and worked at Hamburg and Munich.
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He was a pupil of Surendranath Dasgupta and held a post at Jadavpur University (attested 1977).

Janardan Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, with his tenure attested in 1959 and 1987.
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, where she was supervised by E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College, Newnham College, and under Robert Alexander Neil, later holding a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1898 to 1922.

Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She has held posts at Cornell University, serving as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley and held posts at Amherst College (1987–2001) and Harvard University as Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies (from 2001).

Janet R. Goodwin is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun works in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Frances Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her BA and MA at Cornell and a PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman. She held faculty appointments at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Janice Leoshko is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Susan L. Huntington and is Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teacher Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University under Alex Wayman in 1985.
